beats.say: This week RISE Live gained frames for its visuals, a memory, and a faster swarm.
The attractor can now be a swarm of seven hundred particles, and the harmonograph can use two rotary pendulums.
In RISE Live, Sophia now holds every visual in one of three frames, and the visual chooses the frame.
The inner eye holds the harmonograph, ostensoria and apparitio. The outer shell holds the attractor, living flame and turrell.
The full frame holds genesis, fractal, neural, rockgarden, museum images, figures and generated scenes. There, Sophia docks at the left end of the ask bar.
In the full frame, a figure or a generated scene is now fitted clear of the ask bar and the spoken words, so its labels are no longer clipped.
RISE Live now remembers the room within one visit. Each new question goes up with the earlier questions and what RISE said.
So a follow-up like what did Einstein say about it can be understood. Up to six turns go up, and leaving or reloading forgets them.
The page says how many earlier turns were sent, and the privacy text says they go to the provider you chose.
The ask bar now sits at the foot of the room, above the instrument, with the spoken words above it.
On a phone it lifts above the on-screen keyboard. That has only been tried with an emulated keyboard, not a real phone.
A reader who names one of RISE's own visuals during a reading now gets it at once, with no model call. The bar says what is shown.
A fix means that visual reaches the screen at once. Before, it waited for the next phrase, which under a hold took seconds.
The swarm was slow in the venue. It now adds each tick to its trail in one draw. In the shell at 1440 by 900 it rose from 16.4 to 143.9 frames a second.
The flash gate also samples on the GPU now, so only 64 pixels come back.
Live now draws the circle frames at the size they are shown, and the face keeps its trails, as in the approved study.
Those trails now fade back to the ground exactly, so no grey shadow stays in the room.
RISE Changes writes this weekly digest. Claude routes what merged and composes the reading, and RISE's own validators admit it.
The Worker serves the digest files, and the changes pages list and show them.
The team digest now includes every change that matters, read in merge order so a later fix settles an earlier caveat.
A digest is now spoken in RISE's room, from a sealed source that calls no model. That room has no question field.
Each change can now be explained with a picture. The composer writes briefs, and Live's illustrator draws them.
The picture prompts now place things only where the brief says, keep labels clear of each other, and tell the composer the picture room in numbers.
The Node pipeline moved into its own scripts folder, so the core reaches nothing in the live layer. That was the week: frames, memory, a faster swarm, and a digest that speaks and draws.
